page: Microsoft Azure F16alds_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture, operating under Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz, delivering 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs with a single thread per core. Memory provision is 32.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 2.0 GB per core. For high-speed temporary storage, the server includes a 1890 GB local NVMe SSD. Hardware accelerators such as GPUs are absent on this configuration.

Benchmark data reveals exceptional single-threaded compute capabilities. The F16alds_v7 reaches a Geekbench single-core score of 2,845.0 and ranks in the top tier on stress-ng single-core performance with 3,776.28. Vector processing and algorithmic throughput are reinforced by AVX-512 extensions (including VNNI and BF16), producing top-tier results in gzip compression (41.2 GB/sec), bzip3 single-threaded decompression (17.76 GB/sec), image processing, and text processing. Multithreaded synthetic performance remains strong to average, demonstrated by a Geekbench multi-core score of 20,450.0 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 249.41 GB/sec.

Memory bandwidth measurements register 116.72 GB/sec for uncached read-only blocks and 73.34 GB/sec for writes, contributing to a strong PassMark memory benchmark score of 2,767.13. For lightweight machine learning workloads, CPU-driven inference achieves top-tier text generation on small 135M models at 401.18 tokens/sec and strong prompt processing at 3,384.44 tokens/sec, though performance scales down to average tier on 7B models. Storage performance is bolstered by the dedicated 1,890 GB local NVMe SSD, providing high-speed scratch space for I/O-intensive pipelines.

The primary tradeoff of the F16alds_v7 is its low memory density relative to compute cores, limiting its viability for massive in-memory databases or large memory-resident datasets. However, it delivers strong cost efficiency for CPU-bound tasks requiring rapid per-core processing without the overhead of excess memory. Appropriate workloads include CI/CD build environments, batch processing pipelines, web compression, small-scale CPU inference, media transcoding, and compute-focused analytical jobs requiring high local disk throughput.
description: Microsoft Azure F16alds_v7 is a compute-optimized instance configured with 16 dedicated physical cores (16 vCPUs) on an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at 4.5 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture and Microsoft Hyper-V, it features 32.0 GB of system memory (2.0 GB per core) and bundled high-speed storage via a 1,890 GB local NVMe SSD, without a GPU. Benchmark testing highlights top-tier single-core performance, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 2,845.0, top-decile compression throughput, and fast text generation on small language models. Its multi-threaded processing and PassMark CPU metrics maintain strong-to-average ratings across synthetic suites. While the low memory-to-core ratio limits use in large memory-resident databases, the combination of high clock speed and local NVMe storage provides solid cost efficiency for CPU-bound batch operations, software builds, continuous integration pipelines, and media processing tasks.
